text:
Boston arrives having won three of its last five, most recently a 3-2 shootout win over Vegas on Sunday, though we'd call those results a little ahead of the play. The Bruins are +19 in goal difference on only +1.2 in expected goals (the quality of chances), with finishing and goaltending doing the lifting. They're without Matthew Poitras, and Connor Clifton returns to Pittsburgh for the first time since leaving the Penguins. Pittsburgh is winless in three (0-2-1), most recently a 3-2 loss to Vegas when Tomas Hertl scored with 0:35 left. The Penguins are missing Bryan Rust, but Evgeni Malkin has been cleared to return.

The teams are close at five on five, with BOS at 52% of the expected goals and PIT at 53%. Boston takes 4.7 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays. In net, the projected starters are Michael DiPietro (BOS), at +4.3 goals saved above expected over four games, and Arturs Silovs (PIT), at +1.8 this season after -12.8 last year. With Rust out, Tommy Novak has moved onto a line with Crosby and Rakell.

Rickard Rakell has scored in four straight games and sits at 33% to score tonight in our numbers. Sidney Crosby (32%) and Malkin (26%) follow. For Boston, David Pastrnak is our top pick at 35% to score, with 78% for a point. Our under-the-radar pick is Casey Mittelstadt, who has 2.5 expected goals in his last 10 games from third-line minutes. We have him at 21% to score.
